citations.excerpt: in 1800, at a conference near Frederick City, Maryland, the Church was organized under its present name, and Otterbein and Boehm were chosen its first bishops or superintendents.

facts.value: Philip William Otterbein and Martin Boehm

citations.excerpt: under the leadership of Philip William Otterbein (1726–1813), pastor of the Second Reformed Church in Baltimore, and Martin Boehm (1725–1812), a Pennsylvanian Mennonite of Swiss descent.
The ecclesiastical polity of the Church is Wesleyan and its theology is Arminian

facts.value: 1946, main body united into the Evangelical United Brethren Church. A conservative Old Constitution body continues

citations.excerpt: In 1946 the Church of the United Brethren in Christ and the Evangelical Church became the Evangelical United Brethren Church
when the Conservatives, protesting against the new constitution, withdrew and formed the body now commonly known as the United Brethren in Christ “of the Old Constitution.”
